# Adjudication Task — Chapter 54

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃54화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|오래된 TV를 보는 기분이다.
  6|
  7|빛바랜 화면 속 뚝뚝 끊기는 장면과 목소리들. 그럼에도 불구하고 생생하게 느껴지는 전장의 열기.
  8|
  9|‘죽여!’
 10|
 11|‘태원 진가를 멸(滅)하라!’
 12|
 13|좁은 협곡을 빼곡하게 메운 이들이 함성과 함께 돌격한다. 그들의 등 뒤로 항산(恒山)이라 적힌 깃발이 흔들렸다.
 14|
 15|시퍼렇게 날 선 병장기의 끝에, 또 다른 깃발이 있다.
 16|
 17|진(振).
 18|
 19|그리고 협곡을 틀어막은 수백의 무인들.
 20|
 21|‘무(武)도, 협(俠)도 없는 놈들이다. 항산검문은 오늘 사라진다!’
 22|
 23|‘쳐라!’
 24|
 25|지지직.
 26|
 27|노이즈와 함께 시야가 확대된다. 태원진가를 상징하는 깃발 아래, 확연히 눈에 띄는 두 사람을 향해.
 28|
 29|흰 수염을 늘어트린 노인이 입을 열었다.
 30|
 31|‘긴 싸움이 되겠군.’
 32|
 33|거대한 덩치의 사내가 대답했다.
 34|
 35|‘그리고 마지막 싸움이 되겠지요.’
 36|
 37|노인이 활짝 웃었다.
 38|
 39|‘그렇게 될 거요. 반드시.’
 40|
 41|이윽고.
 42|
 43|사람과 사람, 검과 창이 부딪친다. 셀 수 없이 많은 무인들이 격돌했고, 협곡에는 짙은 피안개가 깔렸다.
 44|
 45|어디선가 전투의 시작을 알리는 북소리가 울려 퍼졌다.
 46|
 47|둥. 둥. 둥.
 48|
 49|
 50|
 51|* * *
 52|
 53|
 54|
 55|“헉.”
 56|
 57|땀에 젖은 몸을 일으켰다. 또 무림에 관한 꿈이다.
 58|
 59|처음과는 달리 이제는 깨어난 후에도 꿈의 내용을 또렷하게 떠올릴 수 있었다.
 60|
 61|‘전투가 시작됐어.’
 62|
 63|현실로 돌아와도 무림의 시간은 흐른다.
 64|
 65|내가 본 장면들은 지금 무림에서 벌어지고 있는 일인지도 모른다. 두 거대 세력의 명운을 건 대전투.
 66|
 67|‘아니, 하나 더 있지.’
 68|
 69|대장로가 이끄는 제삼의 세력.
 70|
 71|전투가 절정으로 치닫고 양 세력이 큰 피해를 입었을 때, 그때 비로소 놈들이 움직일 것이다.
 72|
 73|‘혁무진은? 정찰조원들은 어떻게 된 거지?’
 74|
 75|그들이 늦지 않게 도착하여 배신을 알린다면 최악의 사태는 면할 수 있다. 어쩌면 그 반대로 이미 모든 게 끝나 있을 수도 있다.
 76|
 77|‘대장로…….’
 78|
 79|첫인상부터 꺼림칙했던 늙은이. 태원진가의 웃어른이라는 작자가 이런 일을 꾸미고 있을 줄이야.
 80|
 81|만약 대장로가 최후의 승자가 된다면 모든 게 끝이다.
 82|
 83|반역의 끝에는 피의 숙청이 뒤따르는 법이니까.
 84|
 85|‘진위경, 위팽, 혁무진과 정찰조원들.’
 86|
 87|거기에 더해 조필과의 싸움에서 중상을 입어 출진하지 못한 한엽, 회복 중인 공야청과 소천, 소율 남매까지.
 88|
 89|낯익은 얼굴들이 떠올랐다 사라지기를 반복한다.
 90|
 91|‘그들은 내게 뭐였지?’
 92|
 93|무림에서의 한 달.
 94|
 95|나는 그들에게 있어 은인이었고, 신뢰하는 상관이자 등을 맡길 수 있는 전우였다. 그리고 누군가에게는…….
 96|
 97|
 98|
 99|‘네가 자랑스럽구나.’
100|
101|‘다친 곳은 없느냐?’
102|
103|‘살아남아라, 막내야.’
104|
105|
106|
107|피를 나눈 형제이기도 했다.
108|
109|하지만 그들은 내게 있어 뭐였을까. 뛰어난 인공지능을 탑재한 NPC? 아니면 사람?
110|
111|‘뭐였을까.’
112|
113|나만이 오갈 수 있는 또 하나의 차원, 그리고 그곳에 남아 있는 사람들. 이걸 어떻게 해야 하나.
114|
115|눈이 저절로 캡슐을 향했다.
116|
117|‘만약에 돌아가면…….’
118|
119|문득 든 생각에 화들짝 놀랐다. 내가 미쳤구나.
120|
121|돌아가면 뭐 어쩌려고? 자그마치 2천여 명의 무림인이 뒤섞인 대전투다. 그중에는 일문일살 조필만큼, 혹은 조필보다 강한 괴물들도 있다.
122|
123|그런데 거기로 돌아가?
124|
125|“이 미친놈. 미친 새끼. 제대로 미쳤어, 아주.”
126|
127|한숨처럼 중얼거리던 그때, 핸드폰이 울렸다.
128|
129|지이잉.
130|
131|
132|
133|[명품충]
134|
135|
136|
137|최 팀장이었다.
138|
139|
140|
141|* * *
142|
143|
144|
145|빌딩 숲 중심부에 위치한 대형 카페.
146|
147|“말씀하신 자료입니다.”
148|
149|김 집사가 두꺼운 서류철을 내밀었다. 대충 보기에도 백여 페이지에 달하는 방대한 분량이다.
150|
151|“많군요.”
152|
153|“그만큼 철저하게 조사했습니다.”
154|
155|최민우는 고개를 끄덕이고 빠르게 페이지를 넘기기 시작했다. 그가 읽고 있는 것은 한 사람의 인생이었다.
156|
157|진태경의 27년이 이 백여 페이지의 종이에 담겨 있다.
158|
159|출생지, 출생 배경과 성장 과정, 심지어는 은행에서 제공한 계좌 조회 기록까지. 없는 게 없었다.
160|
161|특이하거나 의심이 가는 부분은 굵게 칠해져 있었기 때문에 최민우는 불과 30분도 안 되어 준비된 서류를 전부 읽었다.
162|
163|“집사님 생각은 어떠세요?”
164|
165|“깨끗합니다.”
166|
167|김 집사가 확정적인 어조로 대답했다.
168|
169|“부정 각성자도 아니고, 도련님께 계획적으로 접근한 것도 아닙니다.”
170|
171|최민우는 고개를 끄덕였다. 김 집사가 그렇다면 그런 거다.
172|
173|그는 지난 2주 동안 온갖 수단을 동원해 진태경의 모든 걸 들여다본 사람이니까. 마찬가지로, 지금 테이블 위에 놓인 백여 페이지의 서류도 모두 김 집사의 손을 거쳤을 것이다.
174|
175|“그럼 이게 모두 우연이다?”
176|
177|“지금으로서는 그렇습니다.”
178|
179|“집사님.”
180|
181|“예, 말씀하십시오.”
182|
183|“재각성 확률이 얼마나 되는지 알고 계십니까?”
184|
185|“1% 정도로 알고 있습니다.”
186|
187|백 명 중 하나.
188|
189|일반인의 시선에는 그리 희박한 확률이 아닐지도 모른다. 그러나 저 백 명은 일반인이 아닌 헌터다.
190|
191|이미 비슷한 확률을 거쳐 탄생한 헌터들. 그중에서도 선택받은 자들만이 재각성의 행운을 누리는 것이다.
192|
193|“그럼 F급 헌터가 단번에 C급 헌터로 재각성할 확률은 얼마나 될까요?”
194|
195|최민우는 대답을 기다리지 않았다.
196|
197|“C급 헌터가 혼자 동급 게이트를 클리어할 가능성은요?”
198|
199|“혼자라면 불가능합니다. B급 헌터는 되어야…….”
200|
201|“그런데 가능한 사람이 있더군요.”
202|
203|“혹시?”
204|
205|“C급 게이트 10회. D급 게이트 10회. 총합 스무 번의 레이드 동안 제가 한 거라곤 팔짱 끼고 구경한 게 답니다. 나설 필요도 없었어요.”
206|
207|길쭉한 손가락이 두꺼운 서류철을 톡톡 두드렸다.
208|
209|그 안에는 진태경의 모든 게 적혀 있었지만, 한편으로는 아무것도 적혀 있지 않았다.
210|
211|잠시 침묵하던 김 집사가 입을 열었다.
212|
213|“다시 조사해 보겠습니다.”
214|
215|“아닙니다.”
216|
217|최민우가 고개를 저었다.
218|
219|“자꾸 긁으면 부스럼만 생겨요. 계속 곁에 두고 지켜볼 생각입니다.”
220|
221|“결국 길드로 영입할 생각이십니까?”
222|
223|“해야죠. 구린내가 나면 뒤를 캐 보고, 그게 아니면…….”
224|
225|최민우의 눈이 반짝 빛났다.
226|
227|“내 사람으로 만들 겁니다. 삼고초려를 해서라도.”
228|
229|그리고 다음 순간.
230|
231|딸랑.
232|
233|방울 소리와 함께 카페로 들어온 한 사람을 보며 최민우는 피식 웃었다.
234|
235|제갈량, 아니 진태경이었다.
236|
237|
238|
239|* * *
240|
241|
242|
243|계약금 5억.
244|
245|월 5천만 원의 고정 급여와 7할의 정산 비율.
246|
247|40평 상당의 오피스텔과 승용차는 옵션이요, 4대 보험은 기본이다. 계약서를 다 읽고 드는 생각은 딱 하나였다.
248|
249|‘미쳤다.’
250|
251|이런 무지막지한 계약 조건이라니.
252|
253|집도 주고, 차도 주고, 돈은 썩어나게 준다.
254|
255|C급 헌터 평균 연봉이 2억이다. 고정 급여, 레이드 수당을 모두 합쳐서 그렇다.
256|
257|그런데 나는?
258|
259|‘순수 계약금만 5억.’
260|
261|최소 B급 헌터나 받을 수 있는 계약서다.
262|
263|이건 내 실력이 그만큼은 된다는 뜻이기도 하고, 단순하게 헌터를 등급으로만 판단하지 않는 안목 있는 고용주를 만났다는 증거이기도 하다.
264|
265|‘거기에 더해 돈도 있고.’
266|
267|나는 테이블 너머의 최 팀장을 물끄러미 바라봤다. 언제나처럼 속을 알 수 없는 표정에 깊은 눈빛이다.
268|
269|최 팀장이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
270|
271|“이번이 세 번째군요.”
272|
273|그는 앞서 두 번의 계약 제의를 했다. 내가 두 번 다 거절했지만. 이번에는 거절하지 말라는 완곡한 표현이다.
274|
275|“그 부분은 죄송하게 생각합니다. 사소한 문제가 있어서요.”
276|
277|“해결하신 겁니까?”
278|
279|“네. 일단은 그런 것 같네요.”
280|
281|“그럼 이제 아무 문제 없군요.”
282|
283|“……그럼요.”
284|
285|대답하면서도 의문이다. 이제 정말 아무 문제도 없는 걸까. 이대로 괜찮은 걸까.
286|
287|‘내가 도대체 무슨 생각을.’
288|
289|딴생각이 들기 전에 해치워야 한다.
290|
291|“사인하겠습니다.”
292|
293|나는 최 팀장에게 건네받은 만년필로 사인을 시작했다.
294|
295|한 장, 두 장, 세 장…….
296|
297|계약서는 총 다섯 장이었다. 이제 남은 한 장에 이름 석 자를 써 넣으면 끝이다.
298|
299|그 순간, 다시 한번 의문이 떠올랐다.
300|
301|‘이대로 괜찮은 건가?’
302|
303|지금껏 거침없이 움직이던 만년필이 속도를 늦췄다. 생각이 꼬리에 꼬리를 물고 이어졌다.
304|
305|‘괜찮지 않으면? 이게 내가 바랐던 거 아닌가?’
306|
307|맞다. 7년 동안 간절히 꿈꿨던 상황이다.
308|
309|막대한 연봉과 높은 사회적 지위를 얻는 것.
310|
311|자랑스러운 아들, 오빠가 되어 가족들을 호강시켜 주는 것.
312|
313|무시와 경멸 대신 부러움과 선망의 대상이 되는 것.
314|
315|‘이제 다 이룰 수 있어.’
316|
317|저 모든 것들을 누리며 살 수 있다. 구질구질했던 인생도, 개 같은 무림도 안녕이다.
318|
319|빠각.
320|
321|그리고 만년필도 안녕.
322|
323|나는 손아귀의 힘을 풀었다. 박살 난 만년필과 함께 흘러내린 잉크가 계약서를 적셨다.
324|
325|“진태경 씨. 다시 물어보겠습니다.”
326|
327|최 팀장이 흰 손수건을 꺼내 턱에 튄 잉크를 닦아 냈다.
328|
329|갑작스러운 상황에도 그는 침착해 보였다.
330|
331|“지난번 그 문제, 정말 해결됐습니까?”
332|
333|“아뇨.”
334|
335|대답을 하고 나니 속이 후련했다.
336|
337|“혹시 제가 도와드릴 수 있는 문제라면…….”
338|
339|“말씀은 감사합니다만, 저 혼자 해결해야 합니다.”
340|
341|묘한 시선으로 나를 응시하던 최 팀장이 피식 웃었다.
342|
343|“계약이 이렇게 힘든 줄은 몰랐네요. 세 번이나 퇴짜 맞는 것도 예상 못 했고.”
344|
345|화났다기보다는 이 상황이 재미있다는 어투다.
346|
347|“네 번째 제의는 언제쯤 하는 게 좋을까요?”
348|
349|반 농담 삼아 한 말이었겠지만 내 대답은 진지했다.
350|
351|“내일 이 시간, 이 장소에서요.”
352|
353|“내일이요?”
354|
355|“예. 내일.”
356|
357|고작 하루.
358|
359|그러나 내게는 한 달, 혹은 몇 달이 될 것이다.
360|
361|그 사실을 알 리 없는 최 팀장은 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
362|
363|“그런 농담은 별로 안 좋아하는데요.”
364|
365|“저도 안 좋아합니다. 이런 농담.”
366|
367|그는 모른다. 내 말에 어떤 뜻이 담겨 있는지를.
368|
369|“꼭 뵙죠.”
370|
371|이건 스스로에게 하는 다짐이다.
372|
373|반드시 살아 돌아오겠다는 다짐.
374|
375|그리고…….

Zhuge Liang—or rather, Jin Taekyung.

[P111]
* * *

[P112]
A signing bonus of 500 million won.

[P113]
A fixed monthly salary of 50 million won and a seventy-percent settlement share.

[P114]
An officetel of roughly 132 square meters[^2] and a sedan came as extras, while coverage under all four national insurance programs was a given. After reading through the contract, I had exactly one thought.

[P115]
*This is insane.*

[P116]
What kind of outrageous terms were these?

[P117]
They were giving me a home, a car, and more money than I knew what to do with.

[P118]
The average annual income of a C-rank Hunter was 200 million won, including fixed pay and raid earnings.

[P119]
And me?

[P120]
*The signing bonus alone is 500 million.*

[P121]
These terms were normally reserved for B-rank Hunters or higher.

[P122]
That meant they valued my skills that highly. It was also proof that I had found an employer with enough insight not to judge a Hunter by rank alone.

[P123]
*And he has the money to back it up.*

[P124]
I stared across the table at Team Leader Choi. As always, his expression gave nothing away, and his gaze was unreadable.

[P125]
Team Leader Choi suddenly spoke.

[P126]
“This is the third time.”

[P127]
He had made me two offers before, and I had turned them both down. This was his roundabout way of telling me not to refuse him again.

[P128]
“I’m sorry about that. There was a minor issue.”

[P129]
“Have you resolved it?”

[P130]
“Yes. For now, I think so.”

[P131]
“Then there shouldn’t be any problem now.”

[P132]
“…Of course.”

[P133]
Even as I answered, doubt gnawed at me.

[P134]
Was there really no problem now? Was it okay to leave things like this?

[P135]
*What the hell am I thinking?*

[P136]
I needed to get this over with before my thoughts wandered again.

[P137]
“I’ll sign.”

[P138]
I began signing with the fountain pen Team Leader Choi had handed me.

[P139]
One page, two pages, three…

[P140]
The contract was five pages long. All I had to do was write the three characters of my name on the last page, and it would be done.

[P141]
At that moment, the question returned.

[P142]
*Is this really okay?*

[P143]
The fountain pen that had moved without hesitation began to slow. One thought led to another.

[P144]
*What if it isn’t? But isn’t this exactly what I wanted?*

[P145]
It was.

[P146]
This was what I had desperately dreamed of for seven years.

[P147]
A massive salary and high social standing.

[P148]
Becoming a son and older brother my family could be proud of, and giving them a comfortable life.

[P149]
Becoming someone others envied and admired instead of ignored and looked down on.

[P150]
*I can have it all now.*

[P151]
I could spend the rest of my life enjoying all of it. Goodbye to my miserable old life. Goodbye to that shitty Murim.

[P152]
Crack.

[P153]
And goodbye to the fountain pen.

[P154]
I relaxed my grip. Ink spilled from the shattered pen and soaked into the contract.

[P155]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung. Let me ask you again.”

[P156]
Team Leader Choi pulled out a white handkerchief and wiped the ink that had splashed onto his chin.

[P157]
Despite the sudden mess, he looked perfectly calm.

[P158]
“That problem from last time. Have you really resolved it?”

[P159]
“No.”

[P160]
The moment I answered, I felt a weight lift from my chest.

[P161]
“If it’s something I can help you with…”

[P162]
“I appreciate the offer, but I have to handle this myself.”

[P163]
Team Leader Choi studied me with an odd look, then gave a quiet laugh.

[P164]
“I didn’t know signing a contract could be this difficult. I never expected to be turned down three times, either.”

[P165]
He sounded more amused by the situation than angry.

[P166]
“When would be a good time for the fourth offer?”

[P167]
He had probably meant it half as a joke, but my answer was serious.

[P168]
“Tomorrow. Same time, same place.”

[P169]
“Tomorrow?”

[P170]
“Yes. Tomorrow.”

[P171]
Only one day.

[P172]
But for me, it would be a month, or perhaps several.

[P173]
Team Leader Choi had no way of knowing that, and he furrowed his brow.

[P174]
“I don’t much like jokes like that.”

[P175]
“Neither do I.”

[P176]
He had no idea what my words meant.

[P177]
“I’ll see you tomorrow.”

[P178]
It was a vow to myself.

[P179]
A vow that I would return alive.

[P180]
And…

[P181]
“Tomorrow, you’ll have to raise the offer.”

[P182]
I left the café, leaving Team Leader Choi staring after me with wide eyes.

[P183]
* * *

[P184]
“Phew.”

[P185]
I took a deep breath and opened the capsule.

[P186]
The sight of the sagging seat and VR headset made my heart pound. Even after coming this far, temptation kept rearing its head and whispering to me.

[P187]
*Don’t go back.*

[P188]
*Forget everything and be satisfied with your life here.*

[P189]
*Everyone you met in Murim was an NPC, and Murim is nothing more than a game.*

[P190]
Right. There had been a time when I thought that way.

[P191]
But after wrestling with it, I realized that one way or another, I was going back.

[P192]
*I’d already reached my conclusion a long time ago.*

[P193]
On the night of the blizzard, I had gone back for Gong Yacheong.

[P194]
I had brought along two young siblings who were nothing but baggage, and instead of using the reconnaissance squad as shields, I had fought Jopil and nearly died.

[P195]
*It probably started then.*

[P196]
That was when the three letters *NPC*, lodged in my mind, began to fade.

[P197]
That was when I watched Jin Wikyung turn away after telling me to survive and thought of the two-character word *family*.[^3]

[P198]
“Fuck. My life really is a variety show.”

[P199]
With a hollow, bitter laugh, I climbed into the capsule. The moment I put on the VR headset, a single line of text appeared before me.

[P200]
Ding.

[P201]
> **System**
>
> Would you like to log in to Murim?
>
> **Accept** / **Decline**

[P202]
“Yes.”

[P203]
My consciousness faded. My vision went dark.

[P204]
I logged in.

[P205]
[^1]: “Paying three personal visits” alludes to Liu Bei’s repeated visits to Zhuge Liang in *Romance of the Three Kingdoms* to recruit him as an adviser.
[^2]: An officetel is a Korean mixed-use unit designed for both office and residential use.
[^3]: In Korean writing, each syllable is written as a single character block; the word for “family” consists of two such blocks, contrasting with the three Roman letters in “NPC.”
```

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 54

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃54화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|오래된 TV를 보는 기분이다.
  6|
  7|빛바랜 화면 속 뚝뚝 끊기는 장면과 목소리들. 그럼에도 불구하고 생생하게 느껴지는 전장의 열기.
  8|
  9|‘죽여!’
 10|
 11|‘태원 진가를 멸(滅)하라!’
 12|
 13|좁은 협곡을 빼곡하게 메운 이들이 함성과 함께 돌격한다. 그들의 등 뒤로 항산(恒山)이라 적힌 깃발이 흔들렸다.
 14|
 15|시퍼렇게 날 선 병장기의 끝에, 또 다른 깃발이 있다.
 16|
 17|진(振).
 18|
 19|그리고 협곡을 틀어막은 수백의 무인들.
 20|
 21|‘무(武)도, 협(俠)도 없는 놈들이다. 항산검문은 오늘 사라진다!’
 22|
 23|‘쳐라!’
 24|
 25|지지직.
 26|
 27|노이즈와 함께 시야가 확대된다. 태원진가를 상징하는 깃발 아래, 확연히 눈에 띄는 두 사람을 향해.
 28|
 29|흰 수염을 늘어트린 노인이 입을 열었다.
 30|
 31|‘긴 싸움이 되겠군.’
 32|
 33|거대한 덩치의 사내가 대답했다.
 34|
 35|‘그리고 마지막 싸움이 되겠지요.’
 36|
 37|노인이 활짝 웃었다.
 38|
 39|‘그렇게 될 거요. 반드시.’
 40|
 41|이윽고.
 42|
 43|사람과 사람, 검과 창이 부딪친다. 셀 수 없이 많은 무인들이 격돌했고, 협곡에는 짙은 피안개가 깔렸다.
 44|
 45|어디선가 전투의 시작을 알리는 북소리가 울려 퍼졌다.
 46|
 47|둥. 둥. 둥.
 48|
 49|
 50|
 51|* * *
 52|
 53|
 54|
 55|“헉.”
 56|

“I appreciate the offer, but I have to handle this myself.”

[P163]
Team Leader Choi studied me with an odd look, then gave a quiet laugh.

[P164]
“I didn’t know signing a contract could be this difficult. I never expected to be turned down three times, either.”

[P165]
He sounded more amused by the situation than angry.

[P166]
“When would be a good time for the fourth offer?”

[P167]
He had probably meant it half as a joke, but my answer was serious.

[P168]
“Tomorrow. Same time, same place.”

[P169]
“Tomorrow?”

[P170]
“Yes. Tomorrow.”

[P171]
Only one day.

[P172]
But for me, it would be a month, or perhaps several.

[P173]
Team Leader Choi had no way of knowing that, and he furrowed his brow.

[P174]
“I don’t much like jokes like that.”

[P175]
“Neither do I.”

[P176]
He had no idea what my words meant.

[P177]
“I’ll see you tomorrow.”

[P178]
It was a vow to myself.

[P179]
A vow that I would return alive.

[P180]
And…

[P181]
“Tomorrow, you’ll have to raise the offer.”

[P182]
I left the café, leaving Team Leader Choi staring after me with wide eyes.

[P183]
* * *

[P184]
“Phew.”

[P185]
I took a deep breath and opened the capsule.

[P186]
The sight of the sagging seat and VR headset made my heart pound. Even after coming this far, temptation kept rearing its head and whispering to me.

[P187]
*Don’t go back.*

[P188]
*Forget everything and be satisfied with your life here.*

[P189]
*Everyone you met in Murim was an NPC, and Murim is nothing more than a game.*

[P190]
Right. There had been a time when I thought that way.

[P191]
But after wrestling with it, I realized that one way or another, I was going back.

[P192]
*I’d already reached my conclusion a long time ago.*

[P193]
On the night of the blizzard, I had gone back for Gong Yacheong.

[P194]
I had brought along two young siblings who were nothing but baggage, and instead of using the reconnaissance squad as shields, I had fought Jopil and nearly died.

[P195]
*It probably started then.*

[P196]
That was when the three letters *NPC*, lodged in my mind, began to fade.

[P197]
That was when I watched Jin Wikyung turn away after telling me to survive and thought of the two-character word *family*.[^3]

[P198]
“Fuck. My life really is a variety show.”

[P199]
With a hollow, bitter laugh, I climbed into the capsule. The moment I put on the VR headset, a single line of text appeared before me.

[P200]
Ding.

[P201]
> **System**
>
> Would you like to log in to Murim?
>
> **Accept** / **Decline**

[P202]
“Yes.”

[P203]
My consciousness faded. My vision went dark.

[P204]
I logged in.

[P205]
[^1]: “Paying three personal visits” alludes to Liu Bei’s repeated visits to Zhuge Liang in *Romance of the Three Kingdoms* to recruit him as an adviser.
[^2]: An officetel is a Korean mixed-use unit designed for both office and residential use.
[^3]: In Korean writing, each syllable is written as a single character block; the word for “family” consists of two such blocks, contrasting with the three Roman letters in “NPC.”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
